solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unusually large component of motor vehicle

definitions.meaning: a ... crop or harvest is one far bigger than usual
the bar across the front or rear of a car that takes knocks

explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses of one word: an adjective for abundance and the protective bar on a car.

clue.text: Blooming daughter must get locked up, plainly!

indicators.note: locked up means held inside the other word

parts.note: bally and blooming are both mild British euphemisms for bloody

explanation.surface: A girl's imprisonment announced bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: BALLY, like 'blooming', is a dated British intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking without softening or ornament, in a blunt, unadorned way.

clue.text: Fellow embracing Prince's wife? Not a prime minister!

indicators.note: embracing means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: Not a means one A is dropped from the name

parts.note: Camilla, wife of Prince Charles

explanation.surface: A man hugging a royal spouse is told he is no premier.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'Not a prime minister' looks like a denial, but 'Not a' is the deletion signal and 'prime minister' is the definition, ironically so since the man in question held that office.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan was a British premier, so an example of the office.

clue.text: Manager of Beatles records, number one included

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: included means put within the number

parts.note: ten is a number
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Discs by the Fab Four with a chart-topper among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Epstein managed the band through their rise to fame.

clue.text: Look at row on grandstand less full?

parts.note: to scan something is to look it over
a tier is one of the stepped rows of seating in a stand

explanation.surface: A spectator surveys a half-empty row of seats in the stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective for meagre or sparse, so it means having less in it.

clue.text: Denies identity set up in legal documents

indicators.note: in means placed inside the documents

parts.note: contracts are binding legal agreements

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: Someone disputes a false identity planted in court papers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means read upwards, the usual reversal signal for vertical entries.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a claim is to say the opposite of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Particle of dust finally spotted in cell

indicators.note: spotted in means found sitting inside the cell

parts.note: a neuron is a nerve cell

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of dust

explanation.surface: A speck of dust detected in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic constituent of the nucleus with no charge, a kind of particle.

clue.text: Country's one match — winger for Arsenal left out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: left out means a letter is dropped from the match

parts.note: to tally is to match or correspond

indicators.note: a winger is at the edge, so the last letter of Arsenal

explanation.surface: A nation's one game with an Arsenal winger dropped from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Country' stands for 'is'. 'winger for Arsenal' is the outside letter L, dropped from TALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A European nation, a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Wine mature but lacking power? Chuck!

indicators.note: lacking means the power letter is taken away

parts.note: ripe means mature
to sling is to chuck or throw

explanation.surface: A matured wine has lost its strength, so throw it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A white grape and the wine made from it, an example of wine.

clue.text: Insect's place revealed by entomologist ultimately

parts.note: a locus is a place or position, as in locus of a crime

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word entomologist

explanation.surface: A bug expert finally shows where an insect lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Insect' stands for 'is', a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarming grasshopper is a well-known example of an insect.

clue.text: Cruel article penned by trendy philosopher

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as if shut in a pen

parts.note: David Hume, the Scottish Enlightenment philosopher
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fashionable thinker writes a nasty piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking compassion or humanity is a synonym for being cruel.

clue.text: Report of former champion jockey in Midlands city

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word that follows is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Lester Piggott, many times British champion jockey

explanation.surface: News of a famous jockey turns up in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's name is pronounced like the first name LESTER; Lester Piggott was a celebrated British flat-racing jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the East Midlands of England, a direct example of the category named.

clue.text: Travelling around, spot erratic old creature

indicators.note: travelling around suggests the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: On a journey someone spots something unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: A horned dinosaur long extinct, so an ancient animal.

clue.text: Put soldiers around, befitting the Queen?

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the words for put and soldiers the other way about

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Arranging troops in a manner suitable for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the whole run LAYOR backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regal or suited to a monarch is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Name that is seen in capital, say — an entertainer of yesteryear

indicators.note: seen in means placed inside the capital's name

parts.note: London, the UK capital
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
e.g. means for example, like say

explanation.surface: A name spotted in a big city belongs to a performer of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Lonnie Donegan was the British 'King of Skiffle' in the 1950s, a hugely popular singer of that era.
explanation.definitionFit: A once hugely popular skiffle singer, so a performer from earlier decades.

clue.text: New Testament exponent shows energy, one going through the letters

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
a speller goes through a word letter by letter

explanation.surface: An evangelist's energy as he works through correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' suggests mail or epistles, fitting the New Testament, but means alphabet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reads or preaches the Gospel, a term for a New Testament preacher.

clue.text: Cosy tale about ecclesiastical helpers

indicators.note: about here means moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A comfortable story concerning church assistants.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistants to the clergy in services, such as altar servers.

clue.text: Not favouring valley odours? They're not so bad as they have been

definitions.text: They're not so bad as they have been

parts.note: con as in pros and cons, against
a vale is a valley
scents are smells

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the smells drifting up from the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: People recovering from illness are improving, so less poorly than they were.

clue.text: A bony bit between the eyes shows cut

parts.note: the bridge of the nose is the bony ridge between the eyes

explanation.surface: Part of the nose is exposed by an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a wound, fitting the face, but means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text by cutting parts is a synonym for cut.

clue.text: Disgusting refusal is nothing to this person

parts.note: no is a refusal
O looks like zero, nothing
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a refusal as unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive, especially in smell, a synonym for revolting.

clue.text: Conditions in parts of America

definitions.meaning: ... of mind or health are conditions
the fifty member divisions of the USA

explanation.definitionFit: One word naming both a condition and an American political division.

clue.text: Look less than half serious, as one generally inept?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: less than half of the seven letters of serious means its first three

explanation.surface: A lightly serious look marks out a bungler.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually fails is called this, a near synonym for an incompetent.

clue.text: Birds, pale and sickly, landing aboard ship

indicators.note: landing aboard means placed inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: Seabirds looking ill come down on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-necked water birds, an example of birds.

clue.text: Sailors at home occupying temporary accommodation keeping off the rum?

parts.note: AB is able seaman, so ABS are sailors

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside the next piece

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Seamen camping on shore stay off the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refrains from alcohol, and rum stands for drink in general.

clue.text: RIP? Dispense with the slightest sign of grief

parts.note: rip as a verb means tear
to drop something is to dispense with it

explanation.surface: An epitaph on a grave and a token sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP looks like rest in peace, which suits grief, but it is the verb rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop shed from the eye is the smallest outward show of sorrow.

clue.text: Gosh — that's literature? Don't get so excited!

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a book and is told to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom telling someone to calm down and stop being agitated.

clue.text: Opinion about American President's initial apprehension

indicators.note: about means going round the other pieces

parts.note: sense can mean opinion, as in the sense of the meeting

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of President

explanation.surface: Views on a US president's opening move cause unease.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious uncertainty about what will happen is close to apprehension.

clue.text: Knight will go round trailing society woman? Rubbish!

indicators.note: trailing means coming after the society woman

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering society

indicators.note: go round means the title is turned the other way about

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A knight dawdling behind a society lady gets dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish!' reads as an exclamation of disbelief, but it is a plain noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered waste and rubble, a synonym for rubbish in the sense of litter.
